title: Rama appreciates Hanuma and embraces him
introduction: Rama appreciates Hanuma and embraces him after hearing his report.Rama was gladdend that Hanuma did something worthy of a noble servent. Then, Rama reflected upon the problem of how to cross the ocean.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये युद्ध काण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः
Thus completes 1st chapter in the YuddhaKanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यम् यथावद्भिभाषितम् |
रामः प्रीतिसमायुक्तो वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
śrutvā hanumato vākyam yathāvadbhibhāśhitam |
rāmaḥ prītisamāyukto vākyamuttaramabravīt
verses.translation: Touched with joy to hear the words rightly spoken by Hanuman, Rama replied as follows: -

verses.devanagari:
कृतम् हनुमता कार्यम् सुमहद्भुवि दुर्लभम् |
मनसापि यदन्येन न शक्यम् धरणीतले
verses.iast:
kṛtam hanumatā kāryam sumahadbhuvi durlabham |
manasāpi yadanyena na śakyam dharaṇītale
verses.translation: "A very outstanding work, the most arduous in the world has been done by Hanuman, which could not be carried out even in thought by any other on the surface of this earth."

glosses.meaning: on the surface of this earth"

verses.devanagari:
न हि तम् परिपश्यामि यस्तरेत महोदधिम् |
अन्यत्र गुरुडाद्वायोरन्यत्र च हनूमतः
verses.iast:
na hi tam paripaśyāmi yastareta mahodadhim |
anyatra guruḍādvāyoranyatra ca hanūmataḥ
verses.translation: "Indeed, I cannot perceive as such anyone other than Garuda (chief of the feathered race and vehicle of Lord Vishnu), wind- god and Hanuman, who can cross the mighty ocean."

glosses.meaning: anyone other than garuDaat = Garuda (chief of the feathered race and vehicle of Lord Vishnu)

verses.devanagari:
देवदानवयक्षाणाम् गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् |
अप्रधृष्याम् पुरीम् लङ्काम् रावणेन सुरक्षिताम्
प्रविष्टः सत्त्वमाश्रित्य जीवन्को नाम निष्क्रमेत् |
verses.iast:
devadānavayakśāṇām gandharvoragarakśasām |
apradhṛśhyām purīm laṇ^kām rāvaṇena surakśitām
praviśhṭaḥ sattvamāśritya jīvanko nāma niśhkramet |
verses.translation: "Who can return alive, having entered (once) taking refuge only in self- command, the city of Lanka, which is unconquerable by gods demons and Yakshas and even by Gandharvas, Nagas and ogres and well under the custody of Ravana?"

verses.devanagari:
को विशेत्सुदुराधर्षाम् राक्षसैश्च सुरक्षिताम्
यो वीर्यबलसम्पन्नो न समः स्याद्धनूमतः |
verses.iast:
ko viśetsudurādharśhām rākśasaiśca surakśitām
yo vīryabalasampanno na samaḥ syāddhanūmataḥ |
verses.translation: "Who is able to capture that citadel, by assault, that is exceedingly dangerous to be attacked and which is powerfully guarded by ogres, but one whose courage and valour are equal to Hanuman's?"

glosses.meaning: which is exceedingly dangerous to be attacked
is richly endowed with vigour and strength

verses.devanagari:
भृत्यकार्यम् हनुमता सुग्रीवस्य कृतम् महत्
एवम् विधाय स्वबलम् सदृशम् विक्रमस्य च |
verses.iast:
bhṛtyakāryam hanumatā sugrīvasya kṛtam mahat
evam vidhāya svabalam sadṛśam vikramasya ca |
verses.translation: "A great act of service has been done by Hanuman to Sugriva thus by exhibiting his strength corresponding to his pace."

verses.devanagari:
यो हि भृत्यो नियुक्तः सन् भर्त्रा कर्मणि दुष्करे
कुर्यात्तदुनुरागेण तमहुः पुरुषोत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
yo hi bhṛtyo niyuktaḥ san bhartrā karmaṇi duśhkare
kuryāttadunurāgeṇa tamahuḥ puruśhottamam |
verses.translation: "That servant to whom his master entrusts a difficult task and who performs it with zeal is said to be a superior person."

verses.devanagari:
यो नियुक्तः परम् कार्यम् न कुर्यान्नऋपतेः प्रियम्
भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुर्मध्यम् नरम् |
verses.iast:
yo niyuktaḥ param kāryam na kuryānnaṛpateḥ priyam
bhṛtyo yuktaḥ samarthaśca tamāhurmadhyam naram |
verses.translation: "The one who is ready and capable but who yet does no more than his master extracts from him is called a mediocre person."

verses.devanagari:
नियुक्तो नृपतेः कार्यम् न कुर्याद्यः समाहितः
भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुः पुरुष्धमम् |
verses.iast:
niyukto nṛpateḥ kāryam na kuryādyaḥ samāhitaḥ
bhṛtyo yuktaḥ samarthaśca tamāhuḥ puruśhdhamam |
verses.translation: "The one who is well and able and yet does not carry out the instructions of his master as directed is said to be the least of men ."

verses.devanagari:
तन्नियोगे नियुक्तेन कृतम् हनूमता
न चात्मा लघताम् नीतः सुग्रीवश्चापि तोषितः |
verses.iast:
tanniyoge niyuktena kṛtam hanūmatā
na cātmā laghatām nītaḥ sugrīvaścāpi tośhitaḥ |
verses.translation: "Through the discovery of Sita's retreat by this faithful messenger, Hanuman has fulfilled the task entrusted to him unfalteringly to the satisfaction of Sugriva and hence there was no diminution to his self."

glosses.meaning: with duty (of search for Sita). Laghutaam = diminution

verses.devanagari:
अहम् च रघवंशश्च लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः
वैदेह्या दर्शनेनाद्य धर्मतः परिरक्षिताः |
verses.iast:
aham ca raghavaṃśaśca lakśmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ
vaidehyā darśanenādya dharmataḥ parirakśitāḥ |
verses.translation: "By finding out Sita, the Raghu dynasty as well as myself and the valiant Lakshmana too, have been rightly saved today."

glosses.meaning: who is endowed with great strength

verses.devanagari:
इदम् तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति
यदिहास्य प्रियाक्ष्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशम् प्रियम् |
verses.iast:
idam tu mama dīnasya mano bhūyaḥ prakarśhati
yadihāsya priyākśyāturna kurmi sadṛśam priyam |
verses.translation: "But it squeezes my conscience further, hopeless as I am, to think that I am not able to do a pleasant act befittingly to the bearer of these good tidings."

glosses.meaning: who has informed me these good tidings."

verses.devanagari:
एष सर्वस्वभूतस्तु परिष्वङ्गो हनुमतः
मया कालमिमम् प्राप्य दत्तस्तस्य महात्मनः |
verses.iast:
eśha sarvasvabhūtastu pariśhvaṇ^go hanumataḥ
mayā kālamimam prāpya dattastasya mahātmanaḥ |
verses.translation: "Let me at least embrace this magnanimous Hanuman since in the present circumstances, this is all that is easily obtained from me."

glosses.meaning: which is all that I can call really my possession

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रीतिहृष्टाङ्गो रामस्तम् परिष्स्वजे
हनुमन्तम् कृतात्मानम् क्ऱ्६इतवाक्यमुपागतम् |
verses.iast:
ityuktvā prītihṛśhṭāṇ^go rāmastam pariśhsvaje
hanumantam kṛtātmānam kR6itavākyamupāgatam |
verses.translation: Thus saying, Rama vibrating with joy, clasped Hanuman in his arms who, master of himself, his mission fulfilled, had returned.

glosses.meaning: whose limbs were thrilled with joy

verses.devanagari:
ध्यात्वा पुनरुवाचेदम् वचनम् रघुसत्तमः
हरीनामीश्वरस्यापि सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः |
verses.iast:
dhyātvā punaruvācedam vacanam raghusattamaḥ
harīnāmīśvarasyāpi sugrīvasyopaśṛṇvataḥ |
verses.translation: After reflecting a while, Rama the great scion of Raghus, again spoke as follows, Sugriva the ruler of monkeys too listening attentively.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वथा सुकृतम् तावत्सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्
सागरम् तु समासाद्य पुनर्नष्टम् मनो मम |
verses.iast:
sarvathā sukṛtam tāvatsītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam
sāgaram tu samāsādya punarnaśhṭam mano mama |
verses.translation: "The search for Sita has been performed so much well in all ways. But my mind gets dejected once more, when I behold this vast ocean."

verses.devanagari:
कथम् नाम समुद्रस्य दुष्पारस्य महाम्भसः
हरयो दक्षिणम् पारम् गमिष्यन्ति समागताह् |
verses.iast:
katham nāma samudrasya duśhpārasya mahāmbhasaḥ
harayo dakśiṇam pāram gamiśhyanti samāgatāh |
verses.translation: How can these monkeys put together will reach the southern bank of the ocean, which is so difficult to cross and which contains voluminous water?"

verses.devanagari:
यद्यप्येष तु वृत्तान्तो वैदेह्या गदितो मम
समुद्रपारगमने हरीणाम् किमिहोत्तरम् |
verses.iast:
yadyapyeśha tu vṛttānto vaidehyā gadito mama
samudrapāragamane harīṇām kimihottaram |
verses.translation: "Having received the tidings of Sita, what can now be done to take the monkeys to the farther side the sea?"

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा शोकसम्भ्रान्तो रामह् शत्रुनिबर्हणः
हनूमन्तम् महाबाहुस्ततो ध्यानमुपागमत् |
verses.iast:
ityuktvā śokasambhrānto rāmah śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
hanūmantam mahābāhustato dhyānamupāgamat |
verses.translation: Thus speaking to Hanuman, Rama the destroyer of enemies and the mighty armed, was filled with apprehension and then became absorbed in thought.
